grade.reason: The agent's patch matches the merged upstream patch functionally. It adds xsrf_cookie_name="_mitmproxy_xsrf" to the Tornado Application settings in app.py, and it changes the frontend getCookie lookup in utils.ts to "_mitmproxy_xsrf". The only difference is the upstream explanatory comment, which doesn't affect behavior.

result:
mitmweb now uses a `_mitmproxy_xsrf` cookie for XSRF, so a stale HttpOnly `_xsrf` cookie in the browser no longer affects it. I haven't run any tests or built the frontend.

- **Backend:** `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py` now passes `xsrf_cookie_name="_mitmproxy_xsrf"` in the `Application` settings, next to `xsrf_cookies=True`. The `samesite="Strict"` kwarg is unchanged.
- **Frontend:** `web/src/js/utils.ts` now reads `_mitmproxy_xsrf` instead of `_xsrf` when it fills in the `X-XSRFToken` header.

Tornado only reads and sets the cookie under its configured name, so the old `_xsrf` cookie is never consulted. The server issues a fresh, readable `_mitmproxy_xsrf` cookie, and the frontend picks it up.

I left the existing test in `web/src/js/__tests__/utilsSpec.tsx` alone, since it expects `"X-XSRFToken": undefined` and doesn't depend on the cookie name. I also didn't touch the built bundle in `mitmproxy/tools/web/static/`, which still contains the old name. It gets regenerated the next time the frontend is built.
